title: Provenance and reproducibility
summary: Recording where every document and every number came from, so a stranger can verify a claim without trusting the person making it.
what: Provenance is the chain from a published figure back to the raw input that produced it: source URL, checksum, script, commit.
why: A benchmark nobody can re-run is a marketing claim. The corpus is also too large to redistribute, so the manifest has to stand in for the data.
how: Each document records source, identifier, URL, checksum, page count, tenant and licence. Each derived dataset records the script that produced it and the command that regenerates it.
in_this_project: corpus_manifest.json is committed; the 719 MB of raw documents are not. Replay the URL, verify the checksum. Every precomputed interactive dataset carries describes, generated_by.script, generated_by.regenerate and generated_by.commit — 23 of 23 datasets verified as carrying full provenance. Page counts distinguish real page breaks from estimated ones, because a synthesised number presented as measured is a fabrication regardless of intent.

advantages: Large corpora need not be redistributed
Attribution and licensing are recorded per document

pitfalls: Committing derived data without the script that made it
Prose quoting figures that drift from the data beside it
